items.guidance: Inspect standalone/entrypoint.sh for the production server invocation (for example a gunicorn or uwsgi bind address) and confirm it listens on 8000, the detected application port. If it does, add EXPOSE 8000 to standalone/Dockerfile; add ENV PORT only if entrypoint.sh or settings actually read PORT.

Search the helpdesk URL configuration and the standalone settings/urls for an existing ping or status view before adding one. If none exists, add a minimal Django view returning HttpResponse 200 in the standalone project's urls, and make sure it is reachable without login and that ALLOWED_HOSTS or SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT do not block the load balancer probe, using per-path exemptions rather than global changes.

Check what the standalone settings write under /data (likely MEDIA_ROOT for ticket attachments, possibly static files or a SQLite file) and classify each. If the settings already allow django-storages with an S3 backend via environment variables, report those variables mapped to STORAGE_BUCKET and AWS_REGION; otherwise configure the S3 storage backend for media only, conditional on an environment variable so local FileSystemStorage remains the default.

Check whether celery is actually configured in the standalone project (a celery app module, a CELERY_BROKER_URL setting, or a celery invocation in entrypoint.sh or docker-compose.yml) and whether helpdesk tasks such as email polling depend on it. Report the module path and any existing worker or beat command found, or report that celery is unused at runtime and email is fetched another way.
